definitions.explanation: The act of building or constructing something, especially abstract things like systems, relationships, theories, or networks. While it can refer to physical construction, it is most commonly used for building up non-physical things in a systematic way.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいシステムを{構築|こうちく}する。
{信頼|しんらい}{関係|かんけい}の{構築|こうちく}には{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: Building a relationship of trust takes time.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{海外|かいがい}との{販売|はんばい}ネットワークを{構築|こうちく}するために、{各地|かくち}に{事務所|じむしょ}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: The company opened offices in various locations to build a sales network overseas.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{構|こう} (to construct, to set up) + {築|ちく} (to build, to erect). Both characters relate to building, reinforcing the meaning.

USAGE:
Primarily used as a する verb: {構築|こうちく}する. Favored in formal and technical contexts, especially in business, IT, and academic writing. For physical buildings, {建設|けんせつ} or {建築|けんちく} are more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- システムを{構築|こうちく}する: to build a system
- {関係|かんけい}を{構築|こうちく}する: to build a relationship
- ネットワークを{構築|こうちく}する: to construct a network
- {体制|たいせい}を{構築|こうちく}する: to establish a framework
- データベースを{構築|こうちく}する: to build a database

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {建設|けんせつ}: construction (physical structures like roads, buildings)
- {建築|けんちく}: architecture, building construction (physical buildings)
- {構成|こうせい}: composition, structure (how parts make up a whole)
